newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Toatsu unit's output stopped since blast.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Toatsu unit's output stopped since blast.

text.p: Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc said on Wednesday that its unit Nippon Aluminum Alkyls Ltd had stopped production of a catalyst necessary to make polyolefine since an explosion at its plant on July 17.

"The plant has stopped operations since the blast and the investigation is still under way. We cannot say when it will resume operations because we don't know when the investigation will end," a Mitsui Toatsu spokesman said.
Nippon Aluminum Alkyls produces alkyl aluminium, a catalyst used to make polyolefine.
Mitsui Toatsu has a 75 percent stake in Nippon Aluminum Alkyls.
Only one other firm in Japan makes the catalyst although makers outside of Japan can supply it on a large-scale basis, another spokesman for Mitsui Toatsu said in July.
